cards.text: This is the burden Habakkuk the prophet received in a vision. And it doesn't open with a polite little prayer, friend. Habakkuk opens by crying out to the LORD, and he's got QUESTIONS.

cards.question: What's the first thing Habakkuk asks the LORD?

answers.text: How long must I call for help
Why did You choose me for this
Where should I go to speak next

cards.question: True or false: Habakkuk says he cries out to the LORD, "Violence!" but the LORD does not save.

cards.text: I know a little something about waiting on help in the dark. Years in a junk drawer, and every time it opened I thought THIS IS IT, and it was somebody looking for TAPE.
Habakkuk says destruction and violence are right in front of him. Strife keeps going, and conflict is everywhere.

cards.question: Habakkuk asks the LORD why He makes him see iniquity. Then he asks, Why do You tolerate ___?

cards.text: Because of it all, Habakkuk says the law is paralyzed and justice never goes forth. PARALYZED, like a cookie stamper in the back of a drawer: still there, just not doing ANYTHING.

cards.question: Habakkuk says the wicked hem in the righteous. What happens to justice?

cards.text: Now the LORD answers: "Look at the nations and observe—be utterly astounded!" Not mildly surprised, not "huh, neat," but UTTERLY astounded.

cards.question: The LORD says He is doing a work in your days. How hard will it be to believe?

answers.text: You would never believe it even if told
Only the wise will understand it at first
Everyone will see it coming from far away

cards.text: So what's this unbelievable work? The LORD says He is raising up a nation.

cards.question: Which nation does the LORD say He is raising up?

cards.text: The Chaldeans, a people from Babylon (Jeremiah 50:1). The LORD calls them that ruthless and impetuous nation, and they march through the breadth of the earth.

cards.question: Why do the Chaldeans march through the breadth of the earth?

answers.text: To seize dwellings not their own
To find new land to farm in peace
To trade goods with faraway nations

cards.text: Taking homes that aren't theirs, like the coworker who borrows your chair for ONE meeting and three weeks later it's HIS chair, except this is a whole nation and it's houses. The LORD says they are dreaded and feared.

cards.question: True or false: The Chaldeans get their idea of justice from themselves.

cards.text: Then the LORD paints their army: horses swifter than leopards and fiercer than wolves of the night. Their horsemen charge ahead, their cavalry comes from afar, and they fly like a vulture swooping down to devour.

cards.question: Leopards, wolves and a vulture. What do those pictures say about the Chaldean army?

cards.text: All of them come bent on violence, their hordes advancing like the east wind. That word again, friend: violence.

cards.question: The LORD says the Chaldeans gather prisoners like sand. What's that picture saying?

answers.text: More prisoners than anyone could count
Their prisoners slip right through their hands
Their prisoners are left out in the desert

cards.question: The Chaldeans scoff at kings and make rulers an object of scorn. True or false: A strong fortress makes them turn back.

cards.text: They LAUGH at every fortress and build up siege ramps to seize it, and meanwhile I got stuck for YEARS behind one kitchen drawer. Then they sweep by like the wind and pass through.

cards.question: The LORD says the Chaldeans are guilty. Their own ___ is their god.

cards.text: That's where we'll leave it for now, friend. Trust me, this conversation between Habakkuk and the LORD is NOT done.
